p: A city-centre track makes karting easy to fit into a bigger night out. Victoria station is on the doorstep for trains from across the North West, and it's on the Metrolink too, so groups from Bury, Rochdale, Oldham and beyond can arrive without anyone having to drive.

Timing is key. Book your race for the early evening and plan food and drinks for afterwards. You'll want a clear head and quick reactions on the track, and staff won't let anyone race who's been drinking. Get there with time to spare for sign-in and the briefing, and give your group a meeting time that's earlier than the actual race slot.

First-timers should focus on the basics: look ahead to where you want to go, brake in a straight line before each bend and get back on the power smoothly on the way out. Relax your grip, sit back in your seat and don't be surprised when you feel it in your arms afterwards.
If the group's big, book well ahead, because Friday and Saturday evening slots in the city centre are always popular.

When you're done, you're right on the edge of the Northern Quarter and the Green Quarter, so there's no shortage of places to eat. And if the night goes on, Deansgate and Spinningfields are a short walk away for a celebratory drink or two.
